fixes.why: The note says the traveler is wounded 'and not dead', which contradicts the reading's own label and summary (the fall brought death to every person). Both traditions hold that death is passed on.
fixes.fix: Replace the note with: Early Christian readers took the traveler left half dead as a picture of humankind wounded by the fall.

fixes.why: 'not destroyed' is set against the other reading as though it held that sin destroys the person. Reformed readers hold the image marred, not lost, and the contrast is the card's own, not theirs.
fixes.fix: Change the label to: Wounded and healed: the fall brought death and disorder to every person, the image of God remains, and grace heals the will and moves it

fixes.where: readings[1] passages, Genesis 6:5 note and Psalm 51:5 note
fixes.why: Both notes present a Hebrew Scripture as if it said the Christian doctrine, and do not say these holders are the ones who read it so (rule 8). Genesis 6:5 describes the generation before the flood; Psalm 51:5 is part of a psalm of confession.
fixes.fix: Genesis 6:5 note becomes: Cited by these readers for how deep evil runs in the heart; the verse describes the generation before the flood. Psalm 51:5 note becomes: Cited by these readers as the psalmist's confession of a sin present from conception; the verse is part of a prayer of confession.

fixes.why: Catholic teaching also holds that grace goes before the first movement of faith and is offered to all, which is the account this reading gives. As written, Catholics are placed only in the first reading, and that reading does not say grace is offered to all.
fixes.fix: Add 'Catholic' to held_by of reading 3 (so it reads: Wesleyan / Methodist, Baptist / free church, Pentecostal / Charismatic, Anabaptist, Anglican, Catholic). In its summary, after the sentence ending 'and some hold the second reading.', insert: Catholic members hold the grace that goes before in part, and place it with the first reading.

fixes.why: The note names Catholic and Orthodox readers as connecting regeneration with baptism and leaves out Lutherans, who do the same in the Augsburg Confession.
fixes.fix: Change the note to: New birth. Reformed readers place it before faith and as its cause; Catholic, Orthodox and Lutheran readers connect it with baptism; Wesleyan, Baptist and other readers differ in where they place it.

fixes.why: 'not something earned' states a Protestant contrast. Catholic teaching holds that salvation is a gift of grace and also speaks of merit given by grace, so the common ground should not depend on that contrast.
fixes.fix: Replace 'and that salvation is God's gift and not something earned' with: and that salvation is God's gift of grace, received through faith

fixes.why: Reading 2 says the calls to turn 'name what is owed', and reading 3 says they are 'real offers'. The word 'real' implies that the other reading treats the calls as unreal, and 'owed' puts the other reading's terms in the language of debt. Each should state the call in its holders' own terms, in the same register.
fixes.fix: Reading 2 answers: change 'to name what is owed' to 'to name the duty of the hearer'. Reading 3 answers: change 'as real offers that grace lets people accept' to 'as offers that grace lets people accept'.

fixes.where: readings[0] held_by, and the Orthodox sentence of its summary
fixes.why: The Oriental Orthodox churches (Coptic, Ethiopian, Armenian, Syriac) hold ancestral sin in the same form as the Eastern Orthodox, and have very many members in Africa. The card's tradition list leaves them out, so this reading shows only the Greek and Slavic Orthodox.
fixes.fix: Needs a change to the brief's tradition list first. Once 'Oriental Orthodox' is on that list, add it to reading 1 held_by and to the Orthodox sentence of its summary. For Doug to decide; the writer should not add it on its own.

summary: The card's quotes are all exact, and no verdict word appears outside a quote, so the problems are in framing rather than text. Eight fixes would make it fair to every seat I hold, and the one needing a brief change (the Oriental Orthodox) is for Doug to decide.
